Article Title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the Election Commission is handling the appeals process adequately? Yes, they are doing a good job. No, more needs to be done. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: The Election Commission told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls remain pending. The poll panel told the apex court that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

Article Title: BJP must light a diya to atone for its sins: Congress
Article Text:
Kharge and Rahul Gandhi targeted BJP over “malgovernance” and “lighting of diyas”

New Delhi: Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi targeted BJP over "malgovernance" and "lighting of diyas" during its lamp-lighting campaign for PM Narendra Modi's birthday."In Balaghat, more than 30 tribal children have died amid illness, malnutrition and a lack of basic health facilities. The extent of the callousness is such that innocent lives kept slipping away, yet the response remained sluggish, and the govt kept sleeping," Rahul told MP CM Mohan Yadav."Chief minister, if you have found time after lighting lamps and holding celebrations, take a look at the ground reality in the state," he said, while citing spurious medicines and hooch deaths.Kharge cited Maharashtra govt findings of healthcare markups exceeding 2,000%, saying, "on World Patient Safety Day, Modi govt stands exposed for turning patients into prey. Hospitals are charging a staggering 2,841% markup on basic medical consumables like IVs, according to the Maharashtra FDA, exposing the brazen robbery of common patients, especially in private hospitals."He added, "food, retail and wholesale inflation are already very high and burning the pockets of common people. Perhaps, the BJP should light a diya to atone for its pathetic misgovernance and sins."
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi targeted BJP over "malgovernance" and "lighting of diyas" during its lamp-lighting campaign for PM Narendra Modi's birthday. In Balaghat, more than 30 tribal children have died amid illness, malnutrition and a lack of basic health facilities.

Article Title: SC raps CBSE for refusing to exempt Class VI from 3-language policy this year
Article Text:
CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday rapped CBSE for being stubborn in its decision to enforce the three-language policy from this year for Class VI students and forced it to reconsider the decision with a clear mandate, camouflaged as a suggestion, to enforce it from next academic year.CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X, in which the students were to choose three languages of which two must be indigenous. On SC's request, it reconsidered and agreed to enforce it from Class VI onwards from this year while students in Class VII to X were to be governed by the old policy.SC had asked CBSE to reconsider exempting students of Class VI this year.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is dealing with a bunch of petitions challenging the threelanguage policy, including highlighting the inadequacy of textbooks, indigenous subject teachers and infrastructure.When additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench that CBSE is disinclined to exempt Class VI this year and argued, “Let the Class VI students start this year as they would have three more years before appearing in Class X board examination,” the bench said, “It is your cohort who decided that it must be enforced from Class VI without considering the comfort of the Class VI students upon whom you sprung a surprise.“When the notification for enforcing the policy came, the student was already in Class VI. Go back and reconsider. Anyway, the academic year will come to an end in a few months. You enforce it for Class VI students from the 2027-28 academic year,” it said.Bhati agreed to take back the decision for reconsideration. The bench said exempting Class VI students from the policy this year would be without prejudice to CBSE’s right to defend the policy. “The exemption is purely from the aspect of logistics and balance of convenience,” it said.SC said, “There are more contentious issues on what can be considered an indigenous language (Petitioners say English should be considered as one while Centre objects to it) which we will decide later.”It added, “There must be some degree of comfort for the students. Those who would be coming to Class VI next year would know in advance that they must choose languages as per the three-language policy.You can also make it optional for Class VI students with adequate incentives so those who want to conform to the policy can choose to do so.” SC posted the matter for further hearing on Wednesday.
Article Summary: CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X. Supreme Court asked CBSE to reconsider exempting students of Class VI this year. On SC's request, it reconsidered and agreed to enforce it from this year while students in Class VII to X were to be governed by the old policy.

Article Title: Mid-sea collision: Pak vessel was no match to three-times bigger Indian destroyer INS Kolkata
Article Text:
Pakistan's PNS Hunain sustained significant damage after colliding with India's INS Kolkata.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When 2600-tonne Pakistan warship PNS Hunain collided with Indian Navy ’s 7400-tonne destroyer INS Kolkata, three times its weight, on Tuesday evening, the outcome was known as the Pakistani vessel was no match to India’s big warship. The Pakistan offshore vessel was severely damaged and had to return to the harbour whereas, Indian sources said, the Indian destroyer suffered no damage in the collision.In a statement on Thursday, Pak govt said its “Navy was undertaking its biennial exercise SEASPARK-26 when the Indian vessel carried out aggressive manoeuvres in dangerously close proximity to a Pakistani naval ship, resulting in contact between the two vessels”. Its foreign ministry, in a tit-for-tat reaction on Thursday, summoned the Charge d'Affaires of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad and lodged a strong protest.However, Indian defence sources told TOI that it was the “Pakistani ship that closed the Indian warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea at high speed, manoeuvring in an unprofessional and unsafe manner that led to the collision”.Visuals emerging showed PNS Hunain a huge dent on it and the warship had to be sent for repairs. PNS Hunain is aYarmook-class patrol vessel designed for maritime security, surveillance and limited combat capabilities. Commissioned in 2014, PNS Hunain is about 98 metres long.On the other hand, INS Kolkata is 164 metres long and has a maximum speed of 30 knots and is the lead ship of the indigenously designed and constructed Kolkata-class guided missile destroyers. It carries a heavy mix of surface-to-air missiles, anti-ship cruise missiles, rapid-fire guns, and anti-submarine weapons like BrahMos missiles, Barak 8 missiles and close-in weapon system. For anti-submarine warfare, the Indian warship has torpedo launchers, rocket launchers and a bow-mounted sonar system.PNS Hunain would have sunk if INS Kolkata had taken offensive action. “However, despite extreme provocation, the captain of INS Kolkata “had exercised extreme restraint by taking actions to prevent a severe accident from taking place,” the source told TOI.
Article Summary: Pakistani warship PNS Hunain collided with Indian Navy ’s 7400-tonne destroyer INS Kolkata. The Pakistan offshore vessel was severely damaged and had to return to the harbour. Indian sources said, the Indian destroyer suffered no damage in the collision.

Article Title: Vishwakarma Puja: The Day Nobody Touched the Tools
Article Text:

Sources/Reading:

Dipesh Chakrabarty, Rethinking Working-Class History: Bengal 1890–1940 (Princeton University Press, 1989)

Leela Fernandes, Producing Workers: The Politics of Gender, Class, and Culture in the Calcutta Jute Mills (University of Pennsylvania Press, 1997)

On Vishwakarma Puja, remembering a leather factory that honoured a Hindu god with Muslim hands participating and biryani from Park Street. Nobody thought it needed explaining.Few Hindu festivals can be entered in an office calendar years ahead without consulting a panjika, and Vishwakarma Puja, which falls today, is the most dependable of them, because it is pegged to Kanya Sankranti, the last day of Bhadra, a solar date rather than a lunar one, which is why it generally lands on September 17 every year.It seems only right that the god of engineers should keep better time than most gods.He is, by his résumé, the most accomplished contractor in the Hindu universe. Tradition credits him with Lord Krishna's Dwarka, the golden Lanka that Hanuman ji later set alight, the Pandava capital at Indraprastha and the chariots in which the gods flew. What is less remarked upon is how differently India has chosen to picture him. In the west and north-west he is an old, four-armed man with a white beard and a swan for a mount, which scholars read as a nod to Brahma; in the east he is a young, muscular man with a black moustache, no sons in attendance, and an elephant as his vahana, which suggests God Indra instead.West Bengal, a state with no shortage of bearded elders, decided that its engineer should look like a foreman in his prime, which tells you something about who was doing the worshipping.The flying chariots are how Bengal explains its kites, which dot Kolkata's skies on this day. Hindu mythology is full of gods travelling by air, and Vishwakarma is held to have built the vehicles. The skies over Kolkata on this day used to (and perhaps still do to a lesser extent) fill with petkati and chandiyal, and the morning began with the cry of bhokatta from some rooftop where a boy had just cut a rival's string.Held on the last day of Bhadra, the puja also opens the long Sharodiya season, so the kites were, in effect, the city's first announcement that Maa Durga was on her way. In many Bengali homes the day carries a second observance that has nothing to do with machines. Arandhan, tied to Manasa Puja at Bhadra Sankranti, requires that food be cooked the night before and eaten stale the next day, with cooking itself forbidden; the custom has loosened with modern life but survives in Bengal's villages and in Kolkata's suburbs. The folk phrase for it,— cook in Bhadra and eat in Ashwin — is as good a summary as any.The puja's real home, though, was never the household. It is observed mostly on factory floors, where workers pray for safe conditions and for their machines to run well, and shrines go up among the tools themselves. Historians studying Kolkata's working class have argued that this was something the workers made their own; Dipesh Chakrabarty wrote about festivals as a source of solidarity inside hostile workplaces, and Leela Fernandes's ethnography of the jute mills treated the building of Vishwakarma pandals as a space of the workers' cultural autonomy.The leather factory: My family's business was a leather factory on Tiljala Road, right behind Don Bosco School, and on this day the more than four hundred men who worked there, nearly all of them Muslim, did not touch their tools. The work that honoured the god had been done the day before, when the craftsmen who spent the rest of the year shaping leather goods turned to sheets of coloured paper instead, cutting out decorations with a skill that matched their day jobs and a gusto that suggested they found paper the more forgiving material. Everything the day required was prepared on the eve, and on the day itself the hands rested.By the time the priest arrived, the god of craftsmen was presiding over a room that craftsmen, most of whom did not pray to him, had dressed for him. I have never been sure how much of the abstention was reverence and how much was the ordinary pleasure of a working day on which no work was expected, and I suspect the men themselves would have found the question tiresome, which is perhaps the point.Then there was lunch. Many factory feasts on the day were vegetarian, a mutton curry being the mark of the more generous units, and ours had apparently decided that gastronomy in this feast was a competitive sport and opted for biryani. The biryani came from Shiraz on Park Street, which opened in 1941 at the Park Street and Mullick Bazar crossing, specialising in Awadhi food, founded by Mohammed Arshad Ali and Ali Hussain, who had come to Calcutta from Bihar. Calcutta's biryani, as every Calcuttan will tell you at length, came down from Awadh with Wajid Ali Shah's exile, and Shiraz's cook Shamsuddin, who joined in the 1970s and reworked its biryani, is said to have had an ancestor who cooked for the nawab.Consider the arrangement then. A feast for the Hindu god of craft, cooked to a deposed Muslim king's recipe by a kitchen that claims descent from his, eaten by four hundred Muslim leatherworkers and one Bengali Hindu family, on a day when the stoves in half of Bengal's kitchens were not supposed to be lit. The factory had solved Arandhan by outsourcing it to a Park Street restaurant, and nobody, as far as I remember, felt the need to hold a seminar about it. (We'd hold a good many seminars or news channel debates now.)The next morning the god went into the waters of the Hooghly, and the men went back to their benches. The tools, having been worshipped for a day, went back to being worked, which is, if you think about it, the only form of worship a tool has ever asked for.
Article Summary: Vishwakarma Puja falls on Kanya Sankranti, the last day of Bhadra, a solar date rather than a lunar one. It is observed mostly on factory floors, where workers pray for safe conditions and for their machines to run well, and shrines go up among the tools.

Article Title: Trapped in traffic: Exam-bound kids take 2.5 hours to cover 4km in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Schoolchildren faced severe traffic delays on the Varthur-Gunjur stretch.

Poll Vote & Share your view What's the main reason you believe traffic is so congested in the area during school hours? Poor infrastructure Heavy vehicle movement Lack of traffic management 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: Hundreds of school-children commuting along the Varthur-Gunjur stretch of SH-35 endured a harrowing Thursday as severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning and left students stranded on roads for hours while returning home. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic.The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Parents told TOI children reached exam halls anxious after school buses arrived late at pickup points and were subsequently caught in gridlocked traffic.The evening commute was worse. Several students took up to 1.5 hours more to return home. Some schools accommodated affected students by providing extra time to complete exams.The Varthur-Gunjur stretch, part of SH-35, is undergoing infrastructure works being executed by Karnataka Road Development Corporation. However, residents say the corridor continues to be plagued by bottlenecks, damaged road surfaces, large craters and unmanaged traffic, making the daily commute unpredictable. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.Priti Singh, a resident of Candor Landmark Apartments, said the biggest concern was that schools had exams. “It is unbelievable an area contributing significantly to the city’s economy continues to suffer from such poor infrastructure,” she added.Another resident, Pavitra Holla, said children were spending more time in traffic than in classrooms. “Today, some children took nearly 2.5 hours to cover just 4km from school. They are exhausted, parents are worried and there is no end in sight. There are no proper roads, heavy vehicles move during school hours, traffic management is absent and basic infrastructure is missing. Children are forced to sit in dust and traffic for hours,” she said. Holla added that while congestion has been a long-standing issue in the area, conditions have deteriorated in the past two weeks.For some parents, the situation left them with little choice but to abandon school buses and attempt the journey themselves.Swati Kumari, another resident of Candor Landmark, said she waited nearly 45 minutes for her son’s school bus before deciding to take him on a two-wheeler. “My son studies in a school less than 2km away from home. Though his school ends by 2.45pm, he’s been reaching home around 4.30pm in the past month. The scooter ride took me more than an hour to travel barely 1km,” she said.Calling the commute unsafe, Kumari said parents are increasingly worried about putting young children on two-wheelers given recent accidents and the condition of the road.
Article Summary: Severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic. The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.

NEW DELHI: The six-hitting battle between Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has taken an interesting turn in 2026. Abhishek has now moved 10 sixes ahead of Sooryavanshi, with the India opener hitting 96 sixes in all T20 cricket this year compared to the youngster's 86.Abhishek added 11 more sixes to his tally on Thursday, smashing 108 off just 34 balls against Afghanistan in the third and final T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi.His breathtaking knock included a 30-ball century, the fastest T20I hundred by an Indian batter. It was also the fastest century by a batter from a Full Member nation against another Full Member nation.Abhishek leads Sooryavanshi in six-hittingAbhishek's 96 sixes in 2026 are the second-most by an Indian batter in a calendar year in all T20s.His own record stands at 108 sixes, which he hit in 2025. He also hit 87 sixes in 2024.Sooryavanshi's 86 sixes in 2026 are currently fourth on the list.While Abhishek has hit more sixes overall in 2026, Sooryavanshi has cleared the boundary more frequently, hitting one six every 4.99 balls compared to Abhishek's 6.64.Abhishek produced another power-hitting masterclass against Afghanistan.He smashed 108 off just 34 balls, hitting 11 sixes and nine fours.It was his third century in T20Is.Most of his sixes went straight over the bowler's head. He attacked both pace and spin and kept finding the boundary throughout his innings.With India batting first for the first time in the series, Abhishek made full use of the opportunity.He brought up his fifty off just 16 balls before completing his century off 30 balls.Abhishek's 30-ball century was the fastest T20I hundred by a batter from a Full Member nation.He went past the previous mark of 33 balls, jointly held by Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza and New Zealand's Finn Allen.It was also the fastest century by a batter from a Full Member nation against another Full Member nation.Abhishek also broke former India captain Rohit Sharma's record for the fastest T20I century by an Indian. Rohit had scored his century off 35 balls against Sri Lanka in Indore in 2017.Abhishek's 11 sixes against Afghanistan also put him second on the list of most sixes by an Indian batter in a T20I innings.He is behind only his own record of 13 sixes, which he hit against England in Mumbai in 2025.Abhishek's six-hitting helped India race to 100 for no loss in the first six overs.It was India's highest score in the powerplay in T20Is.Sanju Samson also played his part, scoring a fluent 50 off 35 balls for his second successive fifty-plus score.With both India openers in good form, Sooryavanshi has not got an opportunity in the playing XI in the series.Abhishek completed his century in the ninth over.He reached 99 with a powerful pull off Abdullah Ahmadzai before taking a single to bring up his hundred.He then removed his helmet, sat on the ground and celebrated with a meditation pose as the Delhi crowd applauded the special innings.India eventually finished on 221 for seven. Afghanistan restricted India to 37 runs in the final five overs and picked up four wickets during that period.
Article Summary: Abhishek smashed 108 off just 34 balls, hitting 11 sixes and nine fours. His 30-ball century was the fastest T20I century by an Indian batter. It was also the fastest century by a batter from a Full Member nation against another Full Member team.

Article Title: ‘He has to wait’: Gautam Gambhir’s message to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as teenage sensation watches on
Article Text:

The wait continues for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.India head coach Gautam Gambhir made it clear that the 15-year-old batting sensation will have to be patient for his next opportunity in the senior side, despite the excitement surrounding his emergence and the clamour to see him in action on home soil.Sooryavanshi did not feature in any of India's three T20Is against Afghanistan, with Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma retained as the opening combination throughout the series. India completed a 3-0 sweep with a commanding 127-run victory in the final match in New Delhi on Thursday.Gambhir said the decision was based on the performances of players who had already established themselves, rather than Sooryavanshi's age or potential."From Vaibhav’s point of view, it was a very clear conversation that he will have to wait for his opportunity. We know the kind of talent he has and what he can do, but someone who has been performing for the last 2–3 years will always be ahead of someone who has just entered the team," Gambhir said at the post-match press conference.The India coach also stressed that being 15 does not automatically move Sooryavanshi ahead of established players."Whenever he gets his run, he will get a longer run as well. That is what Indian cricket is all about — we want competition and talent in the dressing room, but that’s how cricket goes. Whether you’re a 15-year-old or a 30-year-old, when you have to wait for your opportunity, you have to wait for your opportunity," he added.Gambhir also revealed how difficult it was to leave Samson out of India's England series, while explaining why the team returned to the combination that delivered the 2026 T20 World Cup."I think his [Samson's] talent itself is enough for him to be in the dressing room. I think he’s shown what he’s capable of. Someone doesn’t become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having that talent. So he’s done enough," Gambhir said."Obviously, it was tough—probably the toughest decision I’ve taken in my coaching tenure was leaving him out in that England series, considering how he performed prior to that," he added.Samson repaid the faith with a half-century in the second T20I before scoring another 50 in the series finale, while Abhishek smashed a record-breaking 108 off 34 balls.Gambhir said India deliberately went back to the opening combination that had delivered their World Cup triumph, arguing that a few failures did not make established players ineffective."But again, sometimes you go with player form as well. In this series, we were always very clear from my point of view that we wanted to go back to the combination we had during the World Cup. Because those guys, after three or four failures, do not become bad players," he said."The cricket we’ve played—if a team has gone unbeaten from one World Cup to another and won the World Cup, I’m sure it’s a gun team. Suddenly, it doesn't become a bad team after one or two series, and these guys do not become bad players after two or three failures. That is what these guys have shown here as well," Gambhir added.Sooryavanshi, India's youngest T20I debutant, had scored 42 runs in three matches in England before making a major impact against Zimbabwe, where he finished the series as the leading run-scorer with 151 runs at a strike rate of 196.10 and was named Player of the Series.
Article Summary: Gautam Gambhir says 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his chance. India head coach says Sanju Samson's talent is enough for him to be in the dressing room. India return to opening combination that delivered 2026 T20 World Cup.

Article Title: Jared Young injury update: Mets first baseman transported to hospital after collision with teammate
Article Text:

What does the Jared Young injury mean for the Mets going forward?

Mets first baseman Jared Young was carted off the field and taken to a nearby hospital Thursday night after a jarring collision with starting pitcher Nolan McLean during New York's game against the Philadelphia Phillies. The team confirmed Young was transported for further evaluation but offered a small measure of relief, noting he had feeling in all his extremities. Interim manager Andy Green later revealed a CT scan came back negative, though Young is dealing with concussion symptoms. Mark Vientos replaced him in the lineup for the rest of the game.The play that caused the scare came in the top of the sixth inning. Phillies outfielder Justin Crawford sent a ground ball toward first base, and as McLean sprinted over to field it, his leg appeared to make contact with Young's head just as the first baseman was bending down to pick up the ball. It was the kind of accidental collision that happens fast and looks bad in real time.Young was immediately attended to by medical staff on the field, then carted off on a stretcher. The Citi Field crowd went quiet. By the end of the night, the Mets had updated fans with the hospital transport news, along with the reassuring detail about sensation in his limbs. Green's post-game briefing confirmed the CT scan showed no structural damage, but the concussion symptoms mean Young's availability going forward is uncertain.This is where the incident stings a little more for the Mets. Young was not supposed to be a centerpiece of anything when the season started. He came into 2026 having played just 44 major league games in his career. Thursday was his 103rd appearance of this season alone.He has made the most of every at-bat. Through the Phillies game, Young was hitting .266 with nine home runs, 17 doubles, and 39 RBI. Against right-handed pitching, he has been genuinely tough to get out, putting up a .797 OPS in 250 plate appearances against righties. Mets director of hitting Jeff Albert said it plainly before the season turned painful: "He's been great. I can't say enough good things about what he's done in the box, defense, in the cage, in the room. Just really a pro all the way around. It's great to see him take advantage of the opportunity. The guys that know him, I don't think it's surprising."That kind of praise from someone inside the organization carries weight, especially for a player who spent years bouncing around the fringes of a major league roster.The Mets are 69-83 and well out of the playoff picture in the NL East. There is no championship chase to protect here, but that does not make Young's situation any less significant. He has been one of the few genuine bright spots in what has been a long, disappointing season in New York. Losing him, even temporarily, takes away a bat that earned its place through consistency rather than reputation.The concussion protocol will dictate his timeline. No return date has been announced, and until symptoms clear, he will not be cleared to play. The Mets will monitor him closely, but right now, the health of the player matters far more than anything happening on the field.
Article Summary: Mets first baseman Jared Young was carted off the field and taken to a nearby hospital Thursday night. A CT scan came back negative, though Young is dealing with concussion symptoms. Young was hitting.266 with nine home runs, 17 doubles, and 39 RBI.

Ben Shelton’s rising star in world tennis is rooted in a deep family legacy. His parents, Bryan Shelton and Lisa Witsken Shelton, brought extensive high-level tennis experience into his life, while his older sister, Emma Shelton, completes a close-knit support system that follows him across the globe. From his father’s transition from tour veteran to full-time coach, to his mother’s standout lineage, family fuels every step of the American’s professional journey.Bryan Shelton spent nine years on the ATP tour, earning two singles titles and reaching a career-high world ranking of No. 55. His landmark playing moment came at Wimbledon in 1994, where he advanced to the round of 16 as a qualifier. After retiring, Bryan shifted to coaching, winning an NCAA title with the Georgia Tech women’s team before taking over the Florida Gators men’s program. There, he coached Ben to a national team title in 2021 and an individual NCAA singles title in 2022.In June 2023, Bryan stepped down from college coaching to become Ben's full-time traveling coach on the ATP tour. Ben shared a heartfelt tribute on Instagram to celebrate his dad's collegiate career:"My dad retired from collegiate coaching today. Congrats on everything you’ve accomplished in your 24 years out there.This isn’t a career that’s defined by championships and accolades, but by the people impacted and lives changed. You showed up to work every day and gave a perfect effort. You did things with character and humility no matter the situation. You’ve kept your faith wherever your life has taken you, and always put your family first. There isn’t a better role model for young men trying to find their way in life. The Gator Nation may have suffered a blow with this one, but we always bounce back. That being said, the dream team is back together baby Can’t wait to have you out on tour with me, and see what we can accomplish together."Lisa Shelton was a top junior tennis competitor before pursuing a career in real estate in Gainesville, Florida.Tennis runs deep on her side of the family as well; her late brother, Todd Witsken, was a three-time All-American at USC who achieved world rankings of No. 4 in doubles and No.43 in singles.Ben's older sister, Emma Shelton, born in March 2001, also competed at the NCAA Division I level, playing for South Carolina and Florida. After graduating in 2023 with a degree in finance, she joined Morgan Stanley as an associate. During Wimbledon, Ben made headlines by asking her employer for extra time off so she could stay and watch his run. Morgan Stanley granted the request, allowing Emma to cheer him on alongside their parents.
Article Summary: Bryan Shelton spent nine years on the ATP tour, earning two singles titles and reaching a career-high world ranking of No. 55. His older sister, Emma Shelton, also competed at the NCAA Division I level, playing for South Carolina and Florida. Lisa Shelton was a top junior tennis competitor before pursuing a career in real estate in Gainesville, Florida.

Article Title: Why Naomi Osaka’s tennis outfits mean more than just making a fashion statement
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka (Getty images)

Naomi Osaka’s fashion style blends sport, culture and identity

Naomi Osaka uses fashion to challenge tennis traditions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Naomi Osaka has changed more than the pace of a tennis match. In recent years, the four-time Grand Slam champion has made her entrances part of the spectacle, using clothes, accessories and cultural references to reveal a different side of herself. From dramatic couture-inspired outfits to Japanese influences and NBA-inspired streetwear, Osaka has made the court another place to tell her story.Osaka’s approach to fashion became especially visible as she returned to competition after becoming a mother. Her clothing offered her another way to reconnect with her identity, while collaborations with designers and Nike allowed her to bring ideas from outside tennis into the sport.One of the clearest examples came with a gothic-inspired look that Osaka described as almost like stepping into another character.“I feel like we’re all kind of exploring together. It’s not that I have multiple personalities, but every time I wear a different outfit, it’s like a different character, almost like a video game, where you can select different avatars. And for me, it always feels like whatever story we’re telling and whatever outfit I’m wearing, it’s like a different version of myself.”That idea helps explain why her outfits rarely feel random. They often carry a reference, a memory or a piece of her personality.At the Australian Open, Osaka took that approach even further with a look inspired by a jellyfish. Created with London designer Robert Wun and Nike, the ensemble included a flowing veil, a wide-brimmed hat and a sheer parasol. Butterfly details also nodded to a memorable moment from her past when a butterfly landed on her face during a match.Osaka explained why these moments matter to her beyond the clothes themselves.“When I look back at the players who came before me, I think about how those moments—those looks—have become memories that live forever […] So much of the time, other people get to write our stories for us. This felt like a moment where I could write a little bit of my own.”Her Grand Slam wardrobe has continued to shift with the setting. At Indian Wells, she embraced bold animal print. At Roland Garros, she wore a shimmering gold design that drew inspiration from the Eiffel Tower. Wimbledon brought a more traditional white palette, but Osaka still found room for personal meaning through a Japanese-inspired kimono wrap.“I’ve never thought of the colour white as a restriction”, Naomi said at the pre-tournament press conference, “there are so many different patterns and textures that you can use. It doesn’t hinder me.”She also explained the cultural connection behind her Wimbledon outfit.“My Japanese heritage means a lot to me… so I thought it would be cool to come out in a kimono.”Osaka’s fashion choices have not gone unnoticed. Some traditionalists have questioned whether elaborate walk-on outfits belong in tennis, particularly when players are expected to follow long-established dress traditions.After one match, Laura Siegemund criticised the idea, saying, “I come here to play tennis, not to put on a fashion show.”Osaka has made it clear that pleasing everyone is not the purpose of her style.“There’s a demographic that’s been talking about ‘traditional’ tennis outfits… I don’t do this for them though, they will never get it and I don’t want them to. I do this for the people that are like me”, she addressed on social media. “I don’t mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it. This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it’s happening with my clothes. I’m literally Haitian, it’s in my blood to be this way—as long as the people after me have an easier path, it’s worth it.Her fashion also reflects influences beyond tennis. Osaka has cited NBA icon Allen Iverson as an inspiration, particularly because of the way he helped reshape how basketball players expressed themselves through clothing.At the US Open, Osaka paid tribute to Iverson with a look featuring a grey hoodie, white skirt, armband and headband. She explained his influence simply:“He’s someone that I look up to a lot”, she told reporters at a press conference before the tournament. “He’s kind of done a lot in fashion, whether it’s on purpose or not, but he’s shifted the way that NBA players dress.”For Osaka, fashion has become more than a collection of striking outfits. It gives her control over how she presents herself, connects her sporting career with her heritage and creates memories for fans before a ball is even struck.Her influence now stretches across tennis, fashion and popular culture. Each entrance offers something different, but the message remains consistent: Osaka wants athletes to have room to be themselves, both on the court and beyond it.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka’s fashion style blends sport, culture and identity. The four-time Grand Slam champion uses clothes, accessories and cultural references to reveal a different side of herself. Her approach to fashion became especially visible as she returned to competition after becoming a mother.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “They told me I wasn’t fit enough to play, but my body carried me through this.” - How Taylor Townsend overcame body shaming and racial bias to become tennis champion
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “They told me I wasn’t fit enough to play, but my body carried me through this.” - How Taylor Townsend overcame body shaming and racial bias to become a tennis champion

What happened between Taylor Townsend and the USTA when she was the No. 1 junior

How did Taylor Townsend deal with race, body image and pressure in tennis

How did motherhood change Taylor Townsend’s career after son Adyn was born

How did Taylor Townsend become a Grand Slam champion with Kateřina Siniaková

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Taylor Townsend has come a long way from being a 16-year-old tennis star whose body became a subject of debate inside American tennis. In 2012, Townsend was the No. 1 junior in the world, but the USTA questioned her fitness and stopped its support around the US Open. She paid her own way to New York and still won the junior doubles title. More than a decade later, Townsend became a Wimbledon champion with Kateřina Siniaková in 2024. In 2026, the pair completed their career Grand Slam by winning the US Open, adding another major chapter to Townsend’s story.Townsend was only 16 when she reached the top of the junior rankings in 2012. She had already won the Australian Open junior singles and doubles titles and then added the Wimbledon junior doubles title. Her results made her one of the biggest young names in American tennis.Then came the dispute that changed how she saw the sport.The USTA wanted Townsend to spend time working on her fitness rather than playing at the junior US Open. The organisation’s officials said they were concerned about her long-term health and development. Townsend, however, felt that her body had become the main focus despite what she was achieving on court.There was also another part of the story. Townsend was later found to have low iron and anemia, which had affected her energy. She eventually received medical clearance, but by then the issue had already caused serious damage to her relationship with the organisation. Her mother, Sheila, helped her get to New York.Townsend did not simply attend the tournament. She made the most of the chance she had fought to keep. She reached the junior singles quarterfinals and won the doubles title with Gabrielle Andrews.Years later, Townsend described the experience in The Players’ Tribune in very direct terms:“I was fat, and I was Black, so they took away my dream. Or at least they tried.”She also explained how difficult it was to be judged so publicly as a teenager.“Being a teenage girl, having to talk about her body, her weight, like on a worldwide stage. It was always a topic of conversation.”The USTA dispute did not disappear once Townsend became a professional. The experience followed her as she tried to build a career in a sport where she often felt different from the image people expected an elite player to have.Townsend grew up on Chicago’s South Side and became a Black girl competing at the highest level of junior tennis. Her style was also different. She liked moving forward, attacking at the net and taking the ball early instead of relying only on long baseline rallies.The pressure around her appearance became difficult to separate from tennis itself. In her own account of those years, Townsend said she felt that she was being pushed to fit a certain image instead of being allowed to develop as the player she was.But she did not leave the sport. She kept building her career and eventually became a regular presence on the WTA Tour.That history also helps explain why her later success meant more than another trophy. Townsend was no longer trying to prove that she could fit someone else’s idea of a tennis player. She was playing on her own terms.Townsend became pregnant in 2020 and gave birth to her son, Adyn Aubrey, in March 2021. She then spent about 18 months away from competitive tennis.That break changed more than her schedule. It changed the way she looked at the sport.In a 2025 interview with Women’s Health, Townsend said becoming a mother helped her step away from the pressure she had carried for years. She said she had spent so much of her life trying to prove herself that she needed the distance to understand what she actually wanted from tennis.“Coming back to tennis after having my son, Adyn, really gave me that freedom to grow into the authentic person I am now.”She also explained that motherhood gave her a different sense of purpose.“As a mom, I have a sense of purpose outside of my sport. I know that winning and losing tennis matches isn’t everything.”That change was visible when she returned. Townsend was still ambitious, but tennis was no longer the only thing defining her.She also became more open about the physical and emotional challenges of returning after childbirth. Instead of hiding the difficult parts, she shared parts of the process publicly. That made her comeback different from the one she might have imagined as a teenager.Townsend’s first Grand Slam women’s doubles title finally arrived at Wimbledon in July 2024. She teamed up with Czech star Kateřina Siniaková, and the pair beat Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe in the final.It was Townsend’s first Grand Slam title at the professional level after earlier runner-up finishes at the 2022 US Open and 2023 French Open. The victory came three years after Adyn’s birth.After winning, Townsend kept the reaction simple:“This is my first one, my first Grand Slam title. I’ve been close two other times. To get over the finish line the way that we did, I think we played so well.”The Wimbledon trophy was only the beginning of what became a remarkable partnership. Townsend and Siniaková went on to win the Australian Open in 2025, the French Open in 2026 and then the US Open in September 2026.Their US Open victory completed the career Grand Slam as a team. Townsend’s achievement is now much bigger than the Wimbledon breakthrough that first put her name on a major trophy.For a player who once had to pay her own way to a junior tournament after being told she was not ready, the contrast is hard to miss. Townsend did not change her story by becoming someone else. She kept playing, became a mother, returned to the biggest stages and eventually collected every women’s doubles Grand Slam with Siniaková.
Article Summary: Townsend was 16 when she reached the top of the junior rankings in 2012. She had already won the Australian Open junior singles and doubles titles and then added the Wimbledon junior doubles title. Then came the dispute that changed how she saw the sport. The USTA wanted Townsend to spend time working on her fitness rather than playing at the junior US Open. Townsend was later found to have low iron and anemia, which affected her energy.

Article Title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf bought a 3.5-acre California estate for $23 million; after four years on the market, it sold for $20 million following an initial $24.5 million listing
Article Text:
Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf bought a 3.5-acre California estate for $23 million; after four years on the market, it sold for $20 million following an initial $24.5 million listing

Why did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf pay $23 million for the Tiburon estate

What made Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s California home unusual

Why did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf list the $23 million estate for $24.5 million

How did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s estate finally sell for $20 million

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s former California home took almost four years to sell after the tennis stars put it on the market. The couple had paid about $23 million for the 3.5-acre Roundhill Estate in Tiburon, California, making it a record residential sale in Marin County at the time. They first listed the property for $24.5 million in 2003, but the asking price was cut several times before the estate finally sold for $20 million in 2006. The sale left Agassi and Graf with a $3 million difference before other ownership costs were counted.Andre Agassi had already developed a strong connection with the San Francisco Bay Area before buying the property. He regularly played tournaments in Northern California and liked the idea of having a private place there.In December 2000, Agassi paid about $23 million for the Tiburon estate, which was then one of the biggest residential deals in Marin County. The property had previously belonged to John E. McCaw Jr., the former Cellular One owner.The location was a major part of its appeal. The estate sat on about 3.5 acres above the San Francisco Bay and had views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco skyline. It also came with a six-bedroom, eight-bathroom home and large outdoor areas.SFGate reported in February 2001 that Agassi described the property as a place he had come to love. “Make no bones about it – I travel 30 weeks-plus a year, and this is a place I’ve come to love, and it’s been a vacation place,” he said.At the time, the home was not only a luxury property but also a practical getaway for a tennis player who spent much of the year travelling. Agassi said it would be a part-time vacation home rather than his main base.The estate also had two swimming pools, a tennis court, a squash court and a four-bedroom staff house. Contemporary reports put the main residence at about 10,500 square feet, while other descriptions gave larger figures when additional buildings were included.The tennis connection was hard to miss. The estate had its own tennis court, giving Agassi and Graf a private place to play away from the public.That mattered because both were still closely linked to professional tennis when the property was purchased. Graf had retired in 1999 after winning 22 Grand Slam singles titles. Agassi continued playing for several more years and eventually retired after the 2006 US Open.The property was also built for a large family and frequent guests. Along with the main house, there were separate staff quarters and additional guest space. Reports also mentioned two pools, several spa areas, a hydrotherapy waterfall and a large private lot.The home had already undergone a major renovation before Agassi bought it. It was built in 1976, and John E. McCaw Jr. had carried out the last major renovation in the 1990s.Still, the house did not remain an easy sell later. When the property went back on the market, its older design became one of the issues affecting interest. Listing agent Bill Bullock told the San Francisco Chronicle that the house had a “dated feel,” which made the sale harder.The size and price were another challenge. A buyer needed to be willing to spend tens of millions of dollars on one property, and the pool of people looking at homes at that level was small.By the time the Tiburon home was listed in 2003, the couple’s lifestyle had changed. Graf had been retired from tennis for several years, while Agassi was still competing but was spending much of his time travelling for tournaments and handling his business interests.The couple also lived primarily in Las Vegas, where Agassi had deep family and business ties. That made the California property less useful as an everyday home.Agassi explained the situation during a 2003 interview. “I’m playing the game a lot longer than I thought. We’re still traveling the world,” he said. “A lot of my business is in Las Vegas and it just doesn’t make sense for us to have a place that doesn’t get used.”They initially asked $24.5 million for the property. That was $1.5 million above what Agassi had paid when he bought it.The estate did not find a buyer quickly. It moved on and off the market, and the asking price was reduced more than once. By 2006, the price had fallen to $21 million.The decision to sell was also tied to the cost of keeping such a large property. Bill Bullock said the couple’s advisers wanted Agassi to dispose of the home because it was being used infrequently.After nearly four years on the market, the Tiburon estate finally found a buyer in 2006. The buyer was Stuart Peterson, a Marin County resident and head of the investment firm Artis Capital Management.The final price was $20 million, which was $3 million below the couple’s original purchase price. The deal was reported as one of the largest residential sales in Marin County at the time.The San Francisco Chronicle reported that the property had been difficult to sell partly because there were relatively few buyers for homes priced above $20 million. The estate had already gone through several price reductions before Peterson agreed to the $20 million deal.The sale meant Agassi and Graf did not make money from the California property itself. Based only on the purchase and sale prices, they were down $3 million. Their actual financial result would have been different after taxes, maintenance, insurance and real estate commissions were taken into account.For the couple, however, the sale also ended a chapter that no longer fitted their daily life. Graf had long since left professional tennis, and Agassi was nearing the end of his playing career when the property finally changed hands.Their Tiburon home had started as a private escape with views of the Bay Area and a tennis court of its own. By the time it sold, it had become a property the couple rarely used and one that had spent years searching for the right buyer.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf bought a 3.5-acre California estate for $23 million in December 2000. They first listed the property for $24.5 million in 2003, but the asking price was cut several times before the estate finally sold for $20 million in 2006. The couple had paid about $3 million difference before other ownership costs were counted.

Article Title: "Forcing events on underage kids": Candace Owens calls out Erika Kirk and TPUSA school event after 500-plus students reportedly attend Nampa gathering
Article Text:
Candace Owens and Erika Kirk (Image via Getty Images)

Candace Owens questions TPUSA event at Nampa Christian School

Club America post celebrates 500-plus students and Erika Kirk appearance

Candace Owens has raised questions over a Turning Point USA event at Nampa Christian School after images showed hundreds of students gathered inside a school gym. Owens claimed students were required to attend the event and that parents could not join them. The posts quickly drew a response online, turning the school gathering into a wider debate over youth political outreach and Charlie Kirk ’s legacy.The controversy began after posts from the event circulated on social media. The photos show a large group of students seated inside a gymnasium, while another image shows a student speaking from a stage carrying Club America branding.Owens responded to a post celebrating the turnout and questioned whether students had a choice about attending. She wrote:“The students were forced to attend this event as a school assembly. They could not opt out.The parents were informed they were not allowed to attend alongside with them.It is insane to me that you have administrations forcing events on underage kids and then are trying to spin it to the public as successful club growth.”The claim about compulsory attendance came from Owens, rather than from the school or TPUSA in the material reviewed for this article. Nampa Christian Schools’ official calendar confirms the school was operating its regular schedule on Sept.18, although the calendar does not list the Club America gathering.Turning Point USA describes Club America as its high school student movement and says it has more than 1,200 student-led chapters. The organisation says the programme is designed to encourage students to engage in activism and promote what it describes as freedom-loving American values.The images also show a post from Nikkelle Hudak-Cardoso celebrating the event and highlighting the reported turnout. Her post stated:“500+ OUTSTANDING high school students attended the @TPUSA ClubAmerica Tour Stop at Nampa Christian School this morning! 🔥@MrsErikaKirk delivered a powerful message to this generation of America First leaders. The future is bright! 🇺🇸”The event appears to fit into TPUSA’s broader effort to expand its youth presence. The organisation has publicly promoted student programmes and Club America chapters as part of its work with high school students.The posts also prompted another social media response defending the event and comparing it with Charlie Kirk’s previous outreach to schools. The account Cinema Shogun wrote:“TPUSA is doing school events just like Charlie Kirk did when he was alive.Candace Owens is only upset because she’s not included.While TPUSA is carrying on Charlie’s legacy and having a positive impact on the youth...Candace Owens is stuck in her basement pandering to a low IQ audience of deranged ding bats with no future ahead of them.Thats why she’s mad.”The final post is an individual’s characterization of Owens and does not establish why she objected to the event. TPUSA has said its current programmes are intended to continue aspects of Kirk’s political organising and student outreach. Its official materials also describe Erika Kirk as part of the organisation’s current leadership and programming.At the centre of the dispute is therefore a straightforward but unresolved question: what role should political organisations play inside schools, and how much choice should students and parents have when such events take place? The available posts offer sharply different accounts, while the school’s public calendar does not independently settle the claims about attendance or parental access.
Article Summary: Candace Owens questions TPUSA event at Nampa Christian School. Owens claimed students were required to attend the event and that parents could not join them. The posts quickly drew a response online, turning the school gathering into a wider debate over youth political outreach and Charlie Kirk ’s legacy.

Article Title: ‘Clear message’ for Hardik Pandya: Gautam Gambhir reveals what the all-rounder must do to return to Team India
Article Text:
File Pic: Gautam Gambhir and Hardik Pandya. (AP Photo)

India could play Hardik and Nitish together

Reddy's bowling development excites Gambhir

Abhishek's hundred powers India to 3-0 sweep

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through game time, with the all-rounder currently not part of India's squads after not playing enough cricket since the IPL.Following India's 127-run win over Afghanistan in the third T20I in New Delhi on Thursday, Gambhir said Pandya's immediate priority should be getting back on the field, including through the India A series, before pushing for a return to the senior sides."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs, and he hasn't played a lot of cricket since the IPL, so we don't want to push him into international cricket because international cricket can be extremely tough on your body as well," Gambhir said during the post-match press conference.The India head coach also revealed that the message to Pandya has been straightforward: play, regain match fitness and then push for a place in both white-ball squads."And that was the clear message to him that if he can play that India A series, and then if everything goes well, he can come back and be part of the T20s and the one-day squad as well," Gambhir said.Gambhir's comments also highlighted India's plans to develop more than one seam-bowling all-rounder.Nitish Kumar Reddy, initially included in India's 15-member Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn from the continental event and will instead feature in the ODI series against the West Indies.Gambhir believes the move will give Reddy valuable game time and accelerate his development with the ball ahead of India's future assignments."From Nitish's point of view, it's actually a great thing that he's been withdrawn from the T20 format, and he'll get game time against the West Indies as well," he said. "We know how important a seam-bowling all-rounder will probably be in a year and when we go to South Africa. And once Hardik comes back, obviously it's going to be good."The coach even suggested India could eventually accommodate both Pandya and Reddy in the same playing XI."Sometimes we could even go on to play both of them in the playing 11," Gambhir said, while stressing that Pandya's current bowling workload remains a factor."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs," he added.Gambhir was encouraged by Reddy's progress as a seam-bowling all-rounder and believes having multiple players who can contribute with both bat and ball will give India greater flexibility."I think it's good that we got Nitish now from the Asian Games so that now he can, and you could see the more he bowls, the better he becomes, and we have when you can develop a couple of seam-bowling all-rounders, it will always be handy," Gambhir said.Reddy will now get an opportunity to feature in the ODI series against the West Indies rather than the Asian Games, providing him with additional match exposure.The Hardik discussion came after India completed a commanding 3-0 T20I series sweep over Afghanistan. Abhishek Sharma smashed a record-breaking 108 off just 34 balls as India posted 221/7 in the third match in New Delhi.Ravi Bishnoi and Reddy then claimed three wickets each as Afghanistan were bowled out for 94, their lowest total against India in T20Is and their heaviest defeat in the format.Gambhir, however, said the focus inside the dressing room remained on impact rather than individual milestones."I can sit here and keep talking about his 100, but it's just the impact. The only thing we talk about in that dressing room is how much impact we create with the bat and how much impact we can create with the ball," Gambhir said.India's 100 runs in the powerplay was another major positive for Gambhir."T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets; it's about how much impact you can create," he said. "The biggest positive was we got a 100 in the powerplay that we have never done in my coaching tenure."
Article Summary: Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through game time, says India head coach Gautam Gambhir. Pandya's immediate priority should be getting back on the field, including through the India A series, before pushing for a return to the senior sides. Nitish Kumar Reddy will feature in the ODI series against the West Indies rather than the Asian Games. India completed a commanding 3-0 T20I series sweep over Afghanistan.

Article Title: Stephen Curry’s $137 million Warriors news gets a positive update ahead of two-year max extension with the franchise
Article Text:
Steph Curry reiterates long-term Warriors commitment amid contract talks. Image via: Getty Images

Stephen Curry reaffirms Warriors' commitment amid contract talks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Warriors' cap space could reshape the roster around Curry

Stephen Curry's $137 million extension decision with the Golden State Warriors is edging toward a resolution, and everything coming out of the Bay Area points somewhere favorable for the franchise. Golden State's front office handed the two-time MVP a menu of contract paths back in August, then stepped away and let him work through it without applying pressure. That patience looks like it is paying off, since Curry has quietly made clear he wants to finish his career right where he started.Warriors insider Anthony Slater expects Curry to settle on an answer within the next ten days, well before media day on September 28 in San Francisco. Whichever version of the deal he picks, the guard many consider the engine of this whole era looks locked in on staying.Stephen Curry became extension eligible on August 29, putting a two-year, $136.7 million offer on the table that the front office left entirely in his hands. Slater said Golden State's decision-makers refused to negotiate on dollar figures and instead gave Curry several paths to pick from, ranging from the outright max to a lighter deal that would open up cap room for next summer.He compared it to a waiter setting down a menu and walking away for a few weeks, adding that Stephen Curry will come back to them and tell them what he wants.Curry has been just as direct in his own words. Asked if a free agency tour similar to the one LeBron James took this past offseason held any appeal, the four time champion shut it down without hesitation, saying he's always stated that he wanna be a lifer with Golden State.That line alone strips away most of the uncertainty hanging over the situation. The $137 million star is not shopping himself around. He is deciding how, not whether, he stays.Whatever number Curry eventually signs at will shape how much room Golden State has to work with. If he takes something closer to $40 million a year instead of the full max, the Warriors could unlock somewhere between $64 and $70 million in space once Jimmy Butler's and Draymond Green's contracts come off the books. Even if Curry takes the full max, Golden State should still carry roughly $40 million in flexibility heading into next offseason.Golden State heads to Hawaii for training camp already knowing where this is headed, even if the paperwork isn't signed yet.
Article Summary: Warriors insider Anthony Slater expects Curry to settle on an answer within the next ten days. Curry became extension eligible on August 29, putting a two-year, $136.7 million offer on the table. Slater said Golden State's decision-makers refused to negotiate on dollar figures.

Article Title: Alix Earle's new ad has hidden clues about Braxton Berrios and Tom Brady that fans can't stop decoding
Article Text:
The Alix Earle ad that's making Braxton Berrios and Tom Brady fans go absolutely feral (Getty Images)

What hidden references did fans spot in Alix Earle's new ad?

What is Alix Earle and Tom Brady's relationship history?

Why did Alix Earle and Braxton Berrios break up?

Alix Earle just dropped a skincare ad for her Reale Actives brand, and it has nothing to do with skincare anymore. Fans are picking apart nearly every frame of it, convinced the TikTok star packed in deliberate nods to her NFL ex Braxton Berrios and rumored fling Tom Brady. A deflated football. A live goat walking on set. A jersey number. The internet did not miss any of it. Whether it was intentional or not, Earle has everyone talking again.The ad opens with Earle walking into a backyard barbecue. A background actor in a sleeveless shirt catches a football. She grabs it from him, flashes a grin, and says, "Thanks, babe!" That shirt had "95" printed on it. Berrios was born in 1995. Fans caught it immediately.Then Earle holds the football, asks, "Do things blow up from time to time?" and proceeds to crush it until it deflates. She answers her own question with a dry "Sure" before tossing it aside. The Deflategate reference was hard to ignore. Brady, of course, was at the center of that 2014 scandal, accused of ordering underinflated footballs before the Patriots beat the Colts 45-7 in the AFC Championship Game.And just when fans thought that was all, a goat walks across the shot.Brady has long been called the G.O.A.T. The placement felt far too deliberate to be a coincidence, and fans treated it exactly that way.Earle and Brady first sparked dating speculation on New Year's Eve 2025 when they were spotted at a party in St. Barths. According to People, they were laughing and dancing closely together throughout the night. That alone was enough to set social media off.The rumors picked up again when both attended a private Fanatics Super Bowl party in San Francisco ahead of Super Bowl 2026. A video circulated by gossip page Deauxmoi showed them chatting closely and dancing, and it went viral fast. Brady has not said a word about any of it publicly. Earle, however, has been less coy. On her show, when a guest asked about Brady directly, she smiled and said, "I'm having fun."That was all anyone needed to hear.Earle and Berrios dated for just over two years before calling it quits in December 2025. She opened up about it on TikTok, pointing to scheduling conflicts and the grind of a long-distance relationship as the main reasons. She also said she wanted to put more energy into building her career.Berrios, now with the New York Giants, has stayed quiet on the matter. Earle has not. She used her Netflix docuseries, *Earle Meets World*, to process the split in real time. In the first episode, she and a friend drive to Berrios' home to pick up her things. She told People the experience was "therapeutic" because it gave her room to say what she actually felt. She described going through "so many emotions" during filming, given the breakup had just happened.All episodes of Earle Meets World are currently streaming on Netflix.
Article Summary: Alix Earle dropped a skincare ad for her Reale Actives brand. Fans are convinced the TikTok star packed in deliberate nods to her NFL ex Braxton Berrios and rumored fling Tom Brady. The ad opens with Earle walking into a backyard barbecue. A goat walks across the shot.

Article Title: ‘Body kept in car for 7 hours’: How a Gurgaon meeting with ex-colleague ended in HR professional’s murder
Article Text:
Yuvraj Singh Manchanda. (File Photo, Image Credit: X)

Former colleague, partner arrested

Argument inside car before alleged killing

Yuvraj went to Gurgaon after meeting sisters

Call records, CCTV point to former colleague

Couple allegedly discloses murder

Five-day police custody





NEW DELHI: A 31-year-old HR professional, reported missing by his family after he went to Gurgaon to meet a former colleague, was allegedly murdered, police have said.Delhi Police has arrested the former colleague, Anya Vats, and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva in connection with the alleged murder of Yuvraj Singh Manchanda. Police suspect a financial dispute to be behind the killing.Anya and Sanyam are both from Gurgaon. Police said the couple told investigators that they were married and had a one-year-old son. There are claims that Yuvraj was shot twice inside his own car, but police are verifying the details.Yuvraj lived with his family in Sarita Vihar. He used to work for a prominent real estate developer.“Anya had worked with Yuvraj in 2022 at another prominent real estate developer’s office and was currently unemployed. She was sacked from the company. We have learnt that some financial irregularities may have been the reason for her termination, but this is being verified,” police said.Sanyam too was unemployed, police added.Sources said an argument happened inside Yuvraj’s car, after which he was allegedly murdered. The couple allegedly told police that they kept the body inside the car for at least seven hours while trying to figure out where to dump it.They later allegedly dumped the body in a sewer near their house. Then they fled to Uttarakhand.Yuvraj was missing from Sept 6 but the family lodged the complaint on Sept 11.On Sept 6, he went to a restaurant in Lajpat Nagar around 4pm. His family said he had gone shopping with his sisters before visiting the restaurant. He told the family he had a meeting in Gurgaon.Yuvraj then told his sisters to take a cab home and left for Gurgaon, sources said.According to the complaint, the family spoke to Yuvraj on the phone around 7pm, when he told them that he would be back home by 10pm. After that, his phone seemed to be switched off. The family could not reach him.His sister approached Lajpat Nagar police on Sept 11, following which a missing person FIR was registered.Investigators analysed call detail records, internet protocol data and CCTV footage and found out that Yuvraj had last spoken to Anya and had also told his family that he was going to Gurgaon to meet her.Both Yuvraj’s and Anya’s phones were switched off, prompting investigators to now track Anya’s movements. During the investigation, Anya emerged as a prime suspect.Investigators subsequently detected a new mobile number allegedly being used by Anya. Technical surveillance indicated she was in Uttarakhand. A police team was sent there and Anya and Sanyam were apprehended.Police said the two disclosed their involvement in Yuvraj’s murder and told investigators that they had thrown his body into a drain near their house in Gurgaon.The disclosure led investigators to Badshahpur police station in Gurgaon, where an unidentified body was found in a drain on Sept 10. The body was badly decomposed.Police showed the photographs of the body to Yuvraj’s family, who identified him.Anya and Sanyam were arrested and produced in court, which sent them to five days’ police custody.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the killing, the alleged financial dispute, the exact roles of the accused and other aspects of the case, besides collecting forensic and technical evidence.
Article Summary: Yuvraj Singh Manchanda, 31, was reported missing by his family after he went to Gurgaon to meet a former colleague. Delhi Police has arrested the former colleague, Anya Vats, and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva in connection with the alleged murder. Police suspect a financial dispute to be behind the killing.

Article Title: Trouble in Japan! Indian athletes face accommodation, food and transport woes ahead of Asian Games 2026
Article Text:
Nagoya: Commuters walk past a banner ahead of the 20th Asian Games at the railway station in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo/Atul Yadav)

Travel woes for shooters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NAGOYA: Torrential rains battered this city last week, forcing evacuations, disrupting train services and even prompting the rescheduling of some Asian Games events. Step into Nagoya today, though, and there is little sign any of it ever happened.As the city braces for the possibility of Typhoon Dujuan hitting the Aichi-Nagoya coast on Monday next, another storm has been brewing around the organising committee. Sustainability and cost-cutting may have been at the heart of the decision to do away with a traditional Games village, but the arrangement has instead triggered chaos and confusion for hundreds of athletes and officials.For many of the 17,000 athletes and officials arriving in the city, the wait at the airport to get their credentials validated and transport arranged has been at least three hours, with some stranded for as long as 14 hours. Already weary from their journey, they were left waiting at the airport, with food and basic arrangements becoming an issue.The problems, which began earlier in the week, continued on Thursday, two days before the Games officially open on Saturday. The confusion did not end at the airport. Athletes arriving at their accommodation were faced with uncertainty over room allocation, with even the hosts caught up in the mess.A section of the Japanese contingent had to seek alternative arrangements after men and women were allotted shared rooms. Indian Olympic Association officials too faced room-allocation issues and were left without accommodation before alternative arrangements were eventually made. Space has emerged as another concern. While compact accommodation is hardly unfamiliar in Japan, the cramped quarters have taken several contingents by surprise. The Costa Serena cruise ship, docked at Kinjo Pier, is housing around 4,000 athletes.Japan’s deputy chef de mission Hisashi Mizutori acknowledged the problems at a press conference on Thursday. “Since the cruise ship village opened, athletes have been arriving and going through the entry procedures. However, the process took a significant amount of time due to issues with activation of their credentials,” he said.The container-style huts, built with an eye on future use as disaster evacuation facilities, have also come under scrutiny. “There is no space to store luggage and we are not here for few days but three weeks, so it’s a challenge in the containers. The ones built for acclimatisation back home by Sports Authority of India were much bigger,” rued an IOA official, an Asian Games veteran. Food has been another source of discontent. While some contingents found fare difficult to adapt, others complained that quantities were inadequate and were forced to eat outside.Logistical problems continued to hit contingents on Thursday. With venues spread across the region and accommodation located some distance away, athletes have been spending hours on the road and, in some cases, missing scheduled training slots. The Indian shooting team was among those affected.The journey from their accommodation to the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery was expected to take around 75 minutes. Instead, the team took more than two hours to reach the venue after waiting nearly three hours for transport to arrive.By then, the Indians had missed their allotted practice slot and had to wait for other teams to finish before getting their turn. Away from the chaos, Nagoya is preparing to welcome the Asian Games back to Japan after a 32-year gap. The industrial and automotive hub is decked out in Games posters and buntings, with trains, subways and streets carrying the colours of the event.Amid the organisational troubles, locals have stepped up. Impromptu volunteers are helping athletes and visitors to navigate the sprawling venues, decipher an unfamiliar language and even find food
Article Summary: Travel woes for shooters as Asian Games organisers face another storm. Athletes arriving at accommodation faced with uncertainty over room allocation. Japanese contingent had to seek alternative arrangements after men and women were allotted shared rooms. Indian Olympic Association officials too faced room- allocation issues and were left without accommodation.
