Article Text:
India beat Japan by 8 wickets, set up semi-final against Bangladesh (Image: BCCI/)

Shree Charani stars as Japan are bowled out for 57

Shafali and Richa wrap up chase in five overs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Who should be key player of India to watch in the semi-finals against Bangladesh? Shafali Verma Shree Charani Richa Ghosh 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their place in the semi-finals against Bangladesh.The result also sets up a repeat of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final line-up, with Sri Lanka set to face Pakistan in the other last-four clash.After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers dismantled Japan’s batting line-up, restricting the hosts to just 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the charge with a remarkable spell of 4/10, including two maiden overs, to register the best bowling figures by an Indian at the Asian Games. Shafali Verma also chipped in with two wickets for 13 runs.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 balls, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships against India’s disciplined attack.India’s chase was emphatic, as they reached the target in just five overs, finishing at 59/2 and winning with 90 balls to spare. Shafali Verma set the tone with a blistering 40 off 15 balls, striking six fours and two sixes.She hammered four boundaries in the opening over and later sealed the victory with a six off Shimako Kato.India had promoted Kamalini and Fulmali up the order, but the move did not pay off, with Kamalini dismissed for a duck and Fulmali scoring six. Shafali then combined with Richa Ghosh, who came in at No. 4, to complete the chase in a hurry.The pair shared a warm hug after the winning hit before crossing over to greet the Japanese players. Japan’s two wickets offered a small positive from an otherwise difficult outing.
Article Summary: India Women beat Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games. Shafali Verma and Richa Ghosh hit half-centuries to set up semi-final clash with Bangladesh. India bowled out Japan for 57 in 19.5 overs, reaching the target in five overs.

Article Title: Separated from their own, these Kuno cheetahs found brothers in each other
Article Text:
An unlikely bond: Male cheetahs CCB4 (left) and KNG23 (right) have come to enjoy each other’s company





BHOPAL: One was born in India while the other flew thousands of kilometres by a special aircraft from Botswana. Though born to different mothers, they are brothers, not by blood but bonding. Deep in the wilds of Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno, two male cheetahs — coded as KNG23 and CCB4 — have developed an unusual social bond, offering a rare insight into how these felines can form lifelong relationships despite not growing up together.Their story, highlighted in the latest newsletter issued by Kuno authorities, has emerged as one of the most unusual behavioural developments in four remarkable years of Project Cheetah.KNG23 was born in India to cheetah Nirva, while CCB4 was among the felines translocated from the African wilds of Botswana. The two unrelated males were brought together after separate periods of isolation. What began as a cautious introduction has evolved into a close social association, with the two now following each other, hunting and feeding together, calling to each other and even grooming one another.The Kuno field team has also observed the two supporting each other when challenged by another coalition.Such behaviour has prompted the team to closely monitor whether their association develops into a stable coalition.Male cheetahs are typically social animals, known to form coalitions, most commonly between brothers from the same litter. Such groups can help males defend territories, hunt and protect kills, patrol their range and confront rivals and predators.KNG23 and CCB4, however, do not fit the familiar pattern. They are unrelated, coming from different countries and growing up in different habitats.However, the stories of how they got separated from their own do bear an uncanny similarity. KNG23 was separated from his mother, brother and sister around March 2026, after suffering a minor injury that required isolation, while CCB4 was separated from his two sisters around the same period.The two males were subsequently introduced to each other.Even after KNG23 recovered and was reunited with his family, he continued to show an interest in CCB4 while the two remained separated by a fence. KNG23 was released into the wild with his mother, brother and sister on May 30. After several weeks, he was injured again in late July and brought back for treatment. By then, CCB4 was alone, as his two sisters had moved into the wild. The two males were again placed close to each other to explore whether their association could develop further.Their first introduction was peaceful. When the fence was removed, both appeared relaxed and comfortable in each other’s presence. The crucial test came when a kill was provided. However, even the prey could put a strain on their relationship, as they both shared the meal without showing any aggression or confrontation.Over the following days, stronger signs of social bonding emerged. KNG23 began following CCB4 closely and sitting beside him. They continued hunting and feeding together. When one moved out of sight, the other responded with the characteristic chirping call used by cheetahs to maintain contact. They were also observed grooming each other, Kuno officials noted in the newsletter.The field team said the two are now displaying several behaviours associated with coalition formation, including remaining together, following one another, hunting and feeding together and mutual grooming.Officials, however, cautioned that sharing a kill or spending time together alone does not establish a coalition. If the association develops into a stable coalition, it could potentially be the first documented coalition between two unrelated male cheetahs originating from different countries, they added.
Article Summary: KNG23 was born in India to cheetah Nirva, while CCB4 was among the felines translocated from the African wilds of Botswana. The two unrelated males were brought together after separate periods of isolation. What began as a cautious introduction has evolved into a close social association.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu on AI doom fears: ‘Without scientific scepticism, we risk being delusional’
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

Sridhar Vembu says AI scepticism must stay grounded in science

James Maynard says he was wrong about AI predictions

Sridhar Vembu says conviction and scepticism both matter

Zoho founder and chief scientist Sridhar Vembu has shared his view on the growing debate over whether AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Sridhar Vembu said he has not bought into AI doom scenarios, but believes people should remain open to changing their views as AI models become more capable. Vembu was responding to a post by American physicist Steve Hsu, who shared comments from Fields Medalist James Maynard on X. Maynard said he had been sceptical of earlier AI predictions that sounded like science fiction but now takes the risks more seriously because many of those predictions have proved more accurate than he expected.Sridhar Vembu said people need both personal conviction and scientific scepticism when thinking about AI and its future.“I have not bought into the AI doom scenarios,” Vembu wrote on X, pointing to Maynard's changing position as an example of what he described as a scientific attitude.“Fields Medalist James Maynard teaches us the scientific attitude about this: he has been highly sceptical of claims of AI doom but as the models demonstrate higher and higher capability levels, he is taking them more seriously now.”Steve Hsu's post quoted Maynard discussing how his view of AI risks has changed.Maynard said he had followed AI for some time but had been sceptical of predictions that appeared to come from science fiction.“I've been interested and I've been following AI, but I've heard all these predictions that just sound like sci-fi and I've been consistently dismissive and skeptical of all of them.”He then acknowledged that his earlier view had been wrong.“But I've been consistently wrong. The people who sound like they're talking from a sci-fi novel are the people who've been making much much more accurate predictions.”Maynard concluded that AI risks should not simply be dismissed as hype.Vembu said personal conviction helps people continue working toward a goal, while scientific scepticism can prevent people from becoming disconnected from evidence.“Our own hunches and convictions allow us to pursue and stick to a course of action and scientific scepticism keeps us grounded in reality,” he wrote.He added:“Without a strong internal conviction, our actions lack the will power to succeed. Without scientific scepticism, we risk being delusional.”
Article Summary: Sridhar Vembu says people need both personal conviction and scientific scepticism when thinking about AI and its future. He was responding to a post by American physicist Steve Hsu, who shared comments from Fields Medalist James Maynard. Maynard said he had been sceptical of earlier AI predictions that sounded like science fiction but now takes the risks more seriously.

Article Title: Offshore wind farms may be quietly stealing rain from Europe's coasts; study says: The more energy turbines pull from the wind, the less...
Article Text:
Representative image

Turbines slow the wind and stir up the air above the sea

Ten years of weather data went into the North Sea rainfall model

The study tested an extreme wind buildout, not Europe's actual plan

Europe is counting on offshore wind to move away from fossil fuels, and the North Sea is at the centre of that plan. The European Union wants 300 gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2050. A new study from Germany suggests turbines at that scale could do more than generate electricity. They could also change where rain falls.Researchers at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon found that very large offshore wind farm clusters may push more rain over the sea and leave parts of the coastline drier. In their simulations, coastal areas in Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom saw rainfall drop by up to 15%. The findings were published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment.A wind turbine works by taking energy out of moving air. The wind behind it ends up slower and more turbulent.That turbulence mixes different layers of the atmosphere. Moist air gets pushed upward, where it cools, condenses and forms clouds. The result is more rain directly over the wind farms.The catch is that air can only carry so much moisture. When more of it falls over the sea, less is left by the time the air reaches land.Coastal regions downwind get less rain as a result.The team at Hereon's Institute of Coastal Systems - Analysis and Modeling used a high-resolution regional climate model called COSMO-CLM. The simulations ran on weather data from 2008 to 2017. Using a full decade smoothed out the effect of any single unusual year and gave a clearer view of long-term patterns.The model included existing wind farms and every zone marked for future development across the North Sea and the Baltic Sea."Our work helps ensure that the further expansion of offshore wind energy in Europe can be aligned with the requirements of climate protection, environmental protection and coastal management," said Dr Naveed Akhtar, the study's lead author.The scenario was extreme by design. The researchers assumed maximum turbine deployment across all designated areas, which pushed installed capacity well past the 300 GW target. The goal was to make any climate effect large enough to detect and measure. It is not a forecast of what Europe will build.The results also describe long-term weather averages. They do not mean a specific town will miss rain on a specific day. Earlier Hereon research has shown that farm size, layout and turbine spacing affect how strongly turbines change the atmosphere, so a smaller or more spread-out buildout may have a milder effect.So will Europe's coasts lose rain? That depends on how the continent builds. The researchers are not arguing against offshore wind. They want more realistic scenarios tested for turbine density, farm size and placement, and they plan to study effects on the ocean and marine life next. For countries that share the same weather systems, where a wind farm goes may matter as much as how much power it produces.
Article Summary: Turbines slow the wind and stir up the air above the sea. Moist air gets pushed upward, where it cools, condenses and forms clouds. The result is more rain directly over the wind farms. When more of it falls over the sea, less is left by the time the air reaches land.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:

RCB register their second win

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old techie fell into a trap by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal's combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Run, explore, date in Delhi's great outdoors
Article Text:
Local runners and triathletes highlight that ditching cars for running shoes turns historic landmarks from mere backdrops into interactive, raw training grounds

‘Green spaces are becoming safe zones’

Traded for booze and late nights, Delhi’s morning raves pair early runs and workouts with live DJ dance floors and craft coffee like this one outside a cafe in Hauz Khas. Starting at dawn, these zero-alcohol events turn Delhi’s iconic spots into fitness festivals

‘If you join the right groups, exercise becomes easier, more enjoyable’

These morning routes turn familiar spaces – from the arches of Lodhi Road to the paths of Deer Park – into a backdrop for both exercise and connection (Pic: @delhiruncollective)

‘Running allows you to see the city that you're in’

Running past India Gate isn’t just about memory; it’s about discipline. Lodhi Road has hostedcountless races and training runs; when you run there, you’re stepping into a legacy of endurance sport in the city Soumya Singh, 27, co- founder of Delhi Run Collective

'With rizz, you can find love anywhere – including run clubs'

For athletes, the city can add to the experience of training





As dawn breaks over Delhi on the weekend, the city’s growing run clubs are reimagining how locals experience their capital. These morning routes turn familiar spaces – from the arches of Lodhi Road to the paths of Deer Park – into a backdrop for both exercise and connection. Running allows the city’s history and greenery to take center stage, far removed from the rush of weekday life. Yet, the run itself is merely the prelude to a larger weekend gathering. As miles turn into post-run breakfasts and casual cafe hangouts, strangers become familiar faces. In these shared weekend spaces, bound by collective effort and easy conversation, Delhi's runners are discovering far more than improved endurance – they are finding a sense of belonging, lasting friendships, and romance.While Gen Z joins the community for social connection, for more fitness-focused members, the runs are a major part of the attraction. Long distance runner and marathon coach Nakul Butta has seen the shift as Gen Z shows up outdoors, “Gen Z is doing runs, especially around places like Nehru Park – it’s convenient, parking is easier, there are bike lanes. Many of them come to hang out as much as to work out.Another way to look at it is that these green spaces are becoming safe zones. ”Soumya Singh, 27, co- founder of Delhi Run Collective shares, “In a city like Delhi, consistency matters, and over time, it translates into real friendships and support systems. The result is not just better fitness; it’s a stronger culture of outdoor movement in a city that needs it.”For athletes, the city can add to the experience of training. Triathlete Sachin Surie, 44, shares, “Delhi can be a great place for outdoor exercise. You just have to know where to go. And if you join the right groups, it becomes much easier and more enjoyable.”Soumya says, “For us, nostalgia fuels performance. Running past India Gate isn’t just about memory; it’s about discipline. Lodhi Road has hosted countless races and training runs; when you run there, you’re stepping into a legacy of endurance sport in the city. These spaces have witnessed marathons, protests, national celebrations, and the daily grind alike. When we train there, it reinforces a simple mindset: keep going. The city has stood the test of time, and so can you.”Soumya believes that the city isn’t just 'pretty sites', but a meaningful training ground for the runners. “The city and its sites aren't a backdrop; it’s the training ground. When our runners lace up early in the morning, Delhi is quieter, cooler, and raw. Running 5K loops around Hauz Khas Lake or clocking miles through Lodhi Garden’s historic greens forces you to experience the city differently, one step at a time. ”Sachin has found a new appreciation for the city since he started running. “As a Dilliwala, you're dependent on your car. But sometimes when preparing for a long run, I'll have to cover the distance on foot. And you see everything slowly. Not like when you're whizzing past in a car; you get to notice more of the city, and you get to view it differently. I love going for a run. You get up early, you go for a run, and you actually get to see the city that you're in. ”Nakul echoes the sentiment. He shares, “We're so blessed in Delhi to have these green open spaces. As runners, we celebrate these spaces and are really grateful to have them. Each area has its own unique appeal and gives you a new perspective when you go out.”Jyotiraditya ‘Joy’ Thakur, 22, co-founder of the Bhag Club, which hosts weekly runs and wellness activities in NCR, shares, “It’s easy to connect with people when you run together. I remember seeing this girl standing alone after a run, so I introduced her to a group of four or five others. The very next week, they were all hanging out together. I’ve also seen people who met here start going for dinners, and eventually even begin dating. It’s been amazing to witness that whole journey – people finding friendships, love, and a sense of belonging at Bhag.”Connecting with fellow runners in Delhi’s open spaces allows for community, especially with social events that come with runs. “Many people living in Delhi aren’t originally from the city. When they attend our events, they naturally begin to connect. Over time, people from different cities really gel with each other. What starts as a shared workout or wellness event turns into something deeper – they become part of one larger community,” shares Rajot Garg, 28, founder of 5 am Social Run Club that works throughout NCR.Joy believes that while it’s not right to label the group as a dating club, it’s always been a part. “I feel like it's okay to find love anywhere. If you are a person who has charisma, enough rizz, you can find people to date even on LinkedIn or your workspace,” adds Joy.
Article Summary: Delhi's growing run clubs are reimagining how locals experience their capital. These morning routes turn familiar spaces – from the arches of Lodhi Road to the paths of Deer Park – into a backdrop for both exercise and connection. Running allows the city’s history and greenery to take center stage, far removed from the rush of weekday life.

Article Title: A night of book lovers: Readers gather for unique night at bookstore; community celebrates shared love for books
Article Text:
A recent bookstore gathering sparked an incredible night of literary connection. Attendees browsed aisles overflowing with books, engaged in enjoyable book-themed activities, and bonded with other literature enthusiasts. This innovative approach transformed the solitary act of reading into a vibrant community event. Participants relished the opportunity to share their favorite stories and gain fresh literary insights, making it a night they would happily relive.

A COMMUNITY BUILT AROUND READING

FROM BOOK HEISTS TO CHARADES

WHEN READING BECOMES AN EXPERIENCE

A NIGHT READERS DIDN’T WANT TO END





What if a night out meant books instead of screens or parties? Last weekend, around 100 readers gathered at a Bandra bookstore from 8 pm to 12.30 am to browse shelves, play book-themed games, meet fellow readers and spend time reading together.Anurag Kothari, co-founder of a book club that has multi-city branches, says, “The idea of spending the night at a bookstore was unique, and the response was tremendous. This has now become a flagship event, and we are taking it to other cities and more venues in Mumbai, as our city has a huge community of book lovers who want more.”For Ekta Bhandari, co founder of the book club ReadAKitab this was a natural extension of what her free book lovers' community has been trying to create for the past five years. “We are a book reading group of over 33,000 readers,” she says. “Our community is about nudging people to read more, read better and read diversely. And this event did just that.” The idea was not simply to put readers in a bookstore at night, but to turn reading into a shared experience. "The carefully curated activities ensured that the evening moved between quiet concentration and lively interaction," said Ekta. Phorum Pandya, a media professional from Juhu and a voracious reader, said, “A book lover’s delight is to find like-minded people to discuss a book they have recently read and to get cool recommendations.My takeaway was meeting people who could hold a book conversation. I love how our city is opening up to social events that go beyond drinking and eating. Go with the idea to have fun.”For Prakhar Sachdeo, a sports content creator from Navi Mumbai who enjoys nonfiction, memoirs, self-help, biographies and sports books, the novelty lay in being around strangers who shared his love for books.“To stay at a bookstore at ungodly hours with few strangers participating in some activities around books and reading was the most fascinating aspect of the event,” he says. But it was the 30-to-35-minute silent reading session that he loved most. “We could read a book of our choice. Meeting new people was fun!”There were challenges, too. Prakhar admits that keeping his energy levels up was one of them. And then there was Book Charades. “Of-course the acting part in our favourite game book-charades was a challenge,” he laughs.The activities became an important part of the night. One involved finding books on the shelves that matched specific descriptions — such as a book whose author’s name began with a particular letter or one with a place in its title.For Arnab, a senior software engineer from Airoli, reading has been a lifelong habit, nurtured by growing up in a Bengali family where reading and asking questions were encouraged. He said the event was both entertaining and enriching. “It was thoroughly enjoyable and enriching at the same time! Book Charades, was way too hilarious with everyone trying to act out the book titles,” he says, adding that the event offered readers a chance “to take a pause in between the daily mundanes. ”Kalpak Chavan, from Borivali West, Vice President at multinational banking institution, enjoys literary fiction, biographies, memoirs and books about ideas, people and society. He says he deliberately avoids restricting himself to one genre. The prospect of spending an entire night in a bookstore immediately caught his imagination. “Bookstores have always felt like spaces where time slows down,” he says. Experiencing one after closing hours, without the usual rush and distractions, felt like “a completely different way of engaging with books. ” “There was something almost magical about being surrounded by shelves of books late at night,” he adds. The activities, he says, created energy and camaraderie among the participants. The biggest challenge? Staying awake. “Reading is usually something I associate with winding down at night, so consciously keeping myself awake and engaged through the night was definitely a challenge. But that was also part of the fun.”For Tony D’Souza, from Goregaon West, a Product Manager at an MNC, the concept itself was the draw. “The concept of being in a bookstore during a night was novel!” he says, listing the group activities, ‘the book heist’, games, silent reading and meeting fellow readers among his favourite parts. His current reading interests include fantasy, literary fiction and manga.For Kinny Shah, a mindful art and creative well-being practitioner from Andheri West, the event was "nothing short of a dream". “I loved to share space and have conversations across different genres, with the community of book lovers from around the city.”Perhaps the most telling measure of the event’s success was the reluctance to leave. “The energy at the event was simply magical: to read in silence with the community, surrounded by books! I didn’t want to leave, didn’t want the night to end.” And perhaps that was the real charm of Night at the Bookstore — it made reading feel less like an individual habit squeezed into a busy day and more like an experience worth staying up for.
Article Summary: Around 100 readers gathered at a Bandra bookstore from 8 pm to 12.30 am to browse shelves, play book-themed games, meet fellow readers and spend time reading together. The idea was not simply to put readers in a bookstore at night, but to turn reading into a shared experience.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.
